acquisition_provenance.metadata_correction: The acquisition workflow carried 2023-09-12 as metadata for RemeGen news id 1731. The archived issuer page itself states Release date: 2023.11.22, so Evidence known-time uses the source-supported 2023-11-22 publication date. Transport metadata never overrides archived source content.

epistemic_guardrails: The 2021 joint release supports announced license/territory terms, not every legal clause of the filed contract; do not silently promote press-release wording to contract-text authority.
RemeGen territory is Asia excluding Japan and Singapore; Japan and Singapore therefore remain outside the retained RemeGen territory in the announced agreement terms.
Pfizer's acquisition of Seagen does not by itself prove that Pfizer replaced Seagen as the named legal licensee under the 2021 agreement.
Pfizer group collaboration, Seagen trial sponsorship and RemeGen collaborator status are distinct roles and must not be collapsed into a generic partner relation.

The 2023 RemeGen urothelial source is a later recap of a 2021 approval. Preserve 2021-12-31 as valid/occurrence time and 2023-11-22/23 as the source's known-time boundary; do not backdate knowledge merely because the event occurred earlier.
Current pipeline and ClinicalTrials registry snapshots establish current operational roles only at their acquisition knowledge vintage unless an older archived version is separately grounded.

authority_profiles.rationale: Joint participant statement directly announces the commercial territory and development allocation, while remaining distinct from the filed contract text.
RemeGen issuer statements are primary for its own approval announcements, pipeline presentation and described collaboration state.
Pfizer Form 10-K is a filed legal disclosure for Pfizer's consolidated R&D and collaboration presentation.
ClinicalTrials.gov is the authoritative registry record for the submitted current lead-sponsor and collaborator fields of NCT05911295.

fragments.excerpt: On June 9th, 2021, National Medical Products Administration(NMPA) announced that China's first independently developed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC)- Disitamab vedotin (trade name: Aidexi®, research code: RC48) was approved to market for the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic gastric cancer (including gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma) with HER2 over-expression in patients who have received at least two types of systemic chemotherapy.

claim_context.scope: locally advanced/metastatic gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, HER2 over-expression, after at least two systemic chemotherapy regimens

fragments.excerpt: Based on these two studies, the urothelial cancer indication of Disitamab Vedotin was approved for marketing in China by NMPA on December 31, 2021.

claim_context.population_context: source discusses HER2-overexpressing (IHC 2+ or 3+) locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma
claim_context.no_lookahead_boundary: This source cannot make the approval replay-visible in 2021; an earlier source would be required for that knowledge vintage.

contradiction_checks.rule: Do not reconcile Pfizer, Seagen and RemeGen into one partner identity. Check role and vintage first: parent/consolidated collaborator, legal licensee, lead sponsor and collaborator are separate claim scopes.
